definitions.definition: The minimum energy needed to excite an electron from the valence band to the conduction band.

definitions.definition: An empty state left in the valence band when an electron leaves a covalent bond; it behaves as a positive carrier and moves opposite to electrons.

definitions.definition: A pure semiconductor crystal without impurities (as defined in the text, fewer than one impurity atom per billion host atoms).

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: Adding a small amount of impurity to an intrinsic semiconductor to increase its conductivity.

definitions.definition: A pentavalent impurity atom that contributes an electron to the conduction band without producing a valence-band hole.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: An extrinsic semiconductor in which electrons are majority carriers and holes are minority carriers.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: An extrinsic semiconductor doped with a trivalent acceptor impurity such as boron or aluminum.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: A trivalent impurity atom that accepts a valence-band electron and creates a hole.

definitions.definition: The PN-junction region depleted of mobile charges, containing separated ions and a potential barrier.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: Connecting P positive relative to N, reducing the junction barrier so majority carriers cross and forward current flows.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: Connecting P negative relative to N; majority carriers do not cross and only a small minority-carrier reverse current flows.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: A forward-biased, heavily doped PN junction that emits photons when electrons recombine with holes.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: A PN-junction diode operated under reverse bias that converts absorbed light into electric current.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: A device that converts light directly into electrical energy by the photovoltaic effect.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: The forward voltage beyond which PN-junction current rises rapidly; 0.3 V for Ge and 0.7 V for Si in the text.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: Conversion of alternating current into direct current; a rectifier performs the conversion.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: The maximum reverse voltage that a rectifying diode must withstand; for the shown half-wave circuit it is V_m.

definitions.definition: A transistor with two PN junctions (NPN or PNP) whose operation involves both majority and minority carriers.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: The heavily doped transistor region that emits charge carriers.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: The thin, lightly doped middle transistor region.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: The transistor region that collects charge carriers.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: Transistor configuration with base common to input and output; emitter is input and collector output.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: The transistor operating region with emitter-base forward biased and collector-base reverse biased.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: The region when both transistor junctions are reverse biased; output current is zero.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: The region when both transistor junctions are forward biased.

definitions.definition: The ratio I_C/I_B and transistor current gain; the dynamic beta factor is ΔI_C/ΔI_B.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: Increasing a signal's strength without changing the original signal.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: In the closed-switch ON state, base and collector current flow and V_CE is approximately zero.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

definitions.definition: In the open-switch OFF state, base and collector currents are zero and V_CE is approximately the supply voltage.

workedExamples.problem: V_CC=10 V, V_C=0.6 V across R_C=500 Ω, α=0.96. Find V_CE, I_B and I_E.
workedExamples.solution: I_C=V_C/R_C=1.2 mA; V_CE=V_CC−V_C=9.4 V; I_E=I_C/α=1.25 mA; I_B=I_E−I_C=0.05 mA.
